newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA TO DECIDE ON GAS CONCESSION NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA TO DECIDE ON GAS CONCESSION NEXT WEEK.

text.p: The Bulgarian government is expected to decide next week on a long-awaited pipeline concession for transiting Russian gas through its territory, Bulgarian officials said on Wednesday.
Energy Minister Roumen Ovcharov, who heads a working group dealing with the issue, said the group's analyses would be distributed to relevant ministers later on Wednesday.
"Within a week our report will be handed over to the government for its final decision," Ovcharov told a news conference. He declined to say how the group had advised the government.

In mid-July the Bulgarian cabinet decided to open a procedure for granting a concession to Bulgarian-Russian joint stock company Topenergy, which was set up in 1995 by Russian gas monopoly RAO Gazprom and Bulgarian gas monopolist Bulgargas.
Bulgarian officials said Gazprom, which holds 50 percent in the joint company, is looking at alternative plans due to Bulgaria's delay in deciding.
Topenergy officials have said the company would need a concession of 30 or 50 years as enlarging the gas transit system on Bulgarian territory was expected to cost some $500 million.
